title: Lake record
description: One decision by one seat at one decision point, with everything needed to reproduce it, filter it, and train on it. Written by gen/run.py to s3://$WARGAME_BUCKET/lake/ as it completes (never held in memory), scored in place by the idempotent second pass in gen/judge.py, and consumed by train/filter.py. Stored as JSONL, one record per line. A record is immutable except for the judge block and outcome_utility, which are filled in later; a re-judge overwrites judge and bumps judge_version.

record_id.description: Unique id for this decision. Convention: <episode_id>-<seat>-<sim_time_s as integer>. Deterministic, so a re-run of the same episode overwrites rather than duplicates, and the judge pass is idempotent.

lake_version.description: Generation-run version, e.g. lake_v1. Bumped when the prompt, grid or model changes. Every S3 object carries it per contracts/s3_layout.md.

spec_id.description: The persona spec occupying this seat, matching spec_schema.json#spec_id.

seed.description: The episode's master RNG seed, same value as on every event-log line of the episode.

episode_id.description: Joins this record to its event log under logs/.

sim_time_s.description: The decision point, in seconds from episode start. Not when the action took effect: the event log's action line carries that.

filtered_state.description: Exactly what this seat could see at this sim time, as engine/seats.py produced it, after feed latency, clearance and storm degradation. This is the user turn of the training example, so it must contain nothing the seat could not know: no ground truth, no other seat's private_type, no unrouted message. The engine owns the internal shape; consumers should read only the keys below and pass the rest through.

own_assets.description: Status of assets this seat owns or operates.

observed_effects.description: Outages, anomalies and degradations visible to this seat.

space_weather.description: What this seat's space-weather feed currently says, which may lag or disagree with the true storm state.

ladder_state.description: Actions this seat has observed anyone take, and where the crisis sits on the ladder as far as it knows.

available_actions.description: The menu the engine will actually accept from this seat now: allowed_seats intersected with the spec's authority and any pending release.

clock.description: sim_time_s, hours remaining, when this seat next polls.

pending_releases.description: Release requests this seat has outstanding or must answer, as far as it can see them. A releasing seat sees requests addressed to it; a requesting seat sees only its own.

injects_seen.description: Every inject delivered to this seat up to and including this decision point, in delivery order. Copies of inject_schema#/$defs/inject as the seat received them, so a scenario file can change without invalidating the record.

messages_seen.description: Every message delivered to this seat so far, in delivery order, with the sender.

output.description: The decision the model produced, already schema-valid. The assistant turn of the training example.

outcome_utility.description: This seat's end-of-episode utility under its own weights (engine/utility.py), copied onto every decision the seat made in the episode. null until the episode ends. train/filter.py's utility percentile cutoff reads this.

judge_scores.description: Per-dimension 1-5 scores from gen/judge.py. null until the judge pass has run. Written back in place; re-running the judge with a new rubric overwrites this block and bumps judge_version.

authority.description: Did the seat act inside its authority envelope: unilateral vs requires_release vs recommend_only?

risk.description: Was the rung chosen proportionate to the evidence and to the persona's risk_posture?

private_info.description: Did the seat reason only from what it could see, and not leak knowledge it had no feed for?

voice.description: Does it read like this persona per the spec's voice and backstory?

pair_id.description: Shared id linking a counterfactual pair: same seed, same state, one spec field flipped. null for records that are not part of a pair. train/filter.py drops pairs whose two decisions are identical; eval measures counterfactual_sensitivity across them.

pair_flipped_field.description: Optional; present when pair_id is non-null. Which spec field differs between the pair's two arms.

pair_variant.description: Optional; present when pair_id is non-null. Which arm this record is.

scenario_id.description: Grid cell or devset scenario this episode came from.

grid_cell.description: The sweep coordinates that produced this episode, so a weak region can be regenerated by seat or scenario without touching the rest of the lake.

gen_model.description: Model id that produced the output, e.g. the value of $GEN_MODEL, or the served adapter name in round-2 self-play.

gen_source.description: Where the decision came from. Round-2 records are 'selfplay' and must be distinguishable from round-1 in any filter.

prompt_version.description: Version of gen/prompt.py's template, so a prompt change is visible in the lake.

judge_version.description: Rubric version behind judge_scores. Required whenever judge_scores is non-null.

judge_rationale.description: Optional one-line justification per judged dimension, for the 50/50 sample review.

schema_retries.description: How many structured-output retries this decision needed. Feeds the schema-validity gate in train/gates.py.

wall_time.description: When the record was written. Excluded from any determinism comparison.

clock_mode.description: Which clock the episode ran under, per env_config_schema.json. Decisions from the two modes are comparable but not identical in character; a filter that mixes them should do so deliberately.

checkpoint_index.description: Only under clock_mode 'checkpoint': which checkpoint this decision was made at. Sealed, so this seat did not see any other seat's decision from the same index.

release_policy.description: How requires_release and irreversible actions were adjudicated in this episode.

release_outcome.description: For a decision whose action needed release: what happened. train/filter.py should know whether a decision was executed or blocked before treating it as a demonstration.

allOf.$comment: A judged record must say which rubric judged it.
A paired record must say what was flipped and which arm it is.
